name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +13 partisan lean
Incumbent Ed Case running with a $1.1M war chest and $600K on hand
Republican Adriel Lam has no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at about 95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Case: a heavily Democratic Honolulu seat, incumbency, and a large financial edge against a Republican challenger with no visible resources. Markets agree, pricing a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at a roughly 22-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Case underperforming his district's lean, or unexpected outside spending for Lam, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's 1st District is a solidly Democratic Honolulu-area seat, and Ed Case is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency and a substantial campaign fund of about $1.1 million raised and $600,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Adriel Lam, shows no reported fundraising, and minor-party candidates Jordan Conley and Nathan Berning are also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Democratic lean, the financial gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 95%. The race is rated Safe D, with Case heavily favored to hold the seat.
